located_facts.label: F2
located_facts.text: [F2] Rectangular reflection class: [[lem-em-rectangular-pec-energy-completeness]] states that the finite separated Fourier modes are dense in the reflection class, that every initial datum of the class has a unique $C(\mathbb R;L^2)$ weak solution of $\partial_tE=(\varepsilon\mu)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}B$, $\partial_tB=-\operatorname{curl}E$ in the class, and that the energy $\frac12\int_Q(\varepsilon|E|^2+|B|^2/\mu)$ is constant along the solution; distributions and their derivatives are those of [[def-distributional-derivative]], and the class is the one of [[def-em-guide-cavity-geometry]] (c); the packaged rectangular branch of [[thm-em-waveguide-spectral-completeness]] (b) repeats these assertions.

located_facts.label: F3
located_facts.text: [F3] Smooth PEC cavity (supplied by the completed in-run items): [[thm-em-waveguide-spectral-completeness]] (a) and [[lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure]] state, under the full Axiom of Choice, that for a bounded $C^\infty$ domain $\Omega$ the graph-norm class $X$ of smooth fields on the closure with $n\times u=0$, its divergence-free subspace $V$ and $H=\overline V^{\,L^2}$ carry a complete orthonormal $L^2$ eigenbasis $\{u_j\}$ of the curl form with nonnegative finite-multiplicity eigenvalues $\lambda_j$, the distributional eigen-equation $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}u_j=\lambda_ju_j$ with the PEC trace, $C^\infty$ eigenfields on the closure, the full-$X$ variational identity $\int_\Omega\operatorname{curl}u_j\cdot\operatorname{curl}v=\lambda_j\int_\Omega u_j\cdot v$ for every $v\in X$, and the associated second-order wave at $v_{\mathrm{wave}}=(\varepsilon\mu)^{-1/2}>0$ for arbitrary $V\times H$ data with $C_tV$ displacement and $C_tH$ velocity. Their statements are the premises used here, and the proof steps below name the supplier consumed at each use.
